IS FILED U/O. 41 RULE 22 OF CPC,
PRAYING TO CALL FOR RECORDS IN MVC NO.705/2011 ON THE FILE OF THE PRL. SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT,
KALABURAGI AND ALLOW THIS CROSS OBJECTION AND MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 22.01.2016 PASSED IN MVC NO.705/2011 BY THE PRL. SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT, KALABURAGI AND ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION FROM RS.9,03,000/- WITH 6% INTEREST TO RS.14,99,000/- WITH 12% INTEREST.

THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT MFA No.200706/2016 is filed by the insurer of one of the vehicles challenging the quantum of compensation while MFA No.200828/2016 is filed by the owner of one of the vehicles challenging the liability imposed upon him

while MFA Crob.N.200069/2017 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi Ganadhar S/O Ramchandra Koti vs Ashok S/O Kalyanrao And Ors on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94411683/
5 (henceforth referred to as 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.705/2011 vide judgment and award dated 22.01.2016.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2. The record of the Tribunal discloses that the claimant, a hotelier and an agriculturist was travelling in a car on 11.09.2008 along with his friend from Kalaburagi to NC: 2023:KHC-K:1368 Humnabad.
When they were on their way, it started raining heavily and they dashed against a lorry bearing registration No.KA-39/6240 parked in the center of the road without switching on the hazard light.
As a result, the claimant suffered injuries and fell unconscious.
He was shifted to Basaveshwar Hospital, where he was treated on 12.09.2008 and then shifted to Yashodhara hospital, Secunderabad, where he was advised to visit KIMS Hospital, Hyderabad.
He underwent treatment from 13.09.2008 to 16.10.2008, during which period, he was operated for closure of wounds of the intestine.
Again he underwent treatment at KIMS hospital, Hyderabad from 11.02.2009 to 19.02.2009.
He thereafter, developed incisional hernia and was again treated at KIMS, hospital Hyderabad between 16.02.2010 to 24.02.2010.
The claimant contended that the injuries suffered by him was permanent and he had difficulty in digesting food.

He therefore,
claimed that he was permanently disabled and hence, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1368 Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of both the vehicles namely, the Car in which he was travelling and the lorry which was parked in the middle of the road.
3. The driver of the lorry was placed ex parte.
4. The insurer of the lorry contested the claim petition and denied the accident and claimed that the lorry was not parked in the middle of the road.
He claimed that as per the charge-sheet, the lorry was moving and the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the car.
It however, admitted that the lorry was insured with it and the policy of the insurance was in force at the time of accident.

5. Respondent No.5 being the owner of the car contended that he had sold the car to the claimant and therefore, he was in noway concerned with the vehicle, as the claimant was deemed to be the owner of the car.
Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
6. The claimant was examined as P.W.1 and he marked Exs.P.1 to P.29.

Two doctors were examined on behalf of the claimant as P.W.2 and 3 who deposed that the claimant had suffered 19% and 55%
to the whole body respectively.

7. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to rash and negligence on the part of the lorry, which was parked in the middle of the road without switching on the hazard lights.

It also held that the claimant had suffered severe injuries in the accident and considering the fact that the claimant was treated from 11.02.2009 till 24.02.2010 in three stages and in view of the evidence of P.W.2 and P.W.3, it assessed the disability suffered by the claimant at 10% to the whole body.

It considered the notional income of the claimant at a sum of Ganadhar S/O Ramchandra Koti vs Ashok S/O Kalyanrao And Ors on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94411683/
6 Rs.7,500/- and - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1368 factored 50% of the income towards loss of future prospects

In so far as the liability to pay compensation is concerned, it held that the drivers of both the vehicles were equally negligent and consequently, 50% of the liability was fastened upon the owner and insurer of the lorry and 50% of the liability was fastened upon the owner of the car.
It directed both of them to pay compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
Being aggrieved by the judgment and award, these appeals are filed.

9. Learned counsel for the insurer in MFA No.200706/2016 contended that the accident - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1368 occurred in the year 2008 and the claimant did not produce any proof that he was running a hotel except Exs.P.1 to P.27.
He submits that these documents did not help in assessing the income of the claimant.
He contended that if notional income as prescribed by this Court is applied, then the notional income of the claimant ought to have been considered at a sum of Rs.4,250/- per month.
He further submitted that the Tribunal having held that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 10%, could not have factored loss of future prospects at 50%.

10. Per contra, learned counsel for the owner of the car submits that the lorry was parked in the middle of the road without switching on any indicators and it was the driver of the lorry who was negligent and therefore, no liability could be fastened on the owner of the car.
11. Learned counsel for the claimant on the other hand submitted that Exs.P.21 to P.23 and P.25 established that the claimant was running a "Khanavali".

Therefore,

7 - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1368 the notional income as fixed by the High Court Legal Services Committee cannot be applied by the Tribunal and the Tribunal was right in considering the notional income at a sum of Rs.7,500/- per month.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also submitted that Exs.P.26 and 27 were the revenue records of the lands that stood in the name of the claimant, which he was cultivating.
Due to the injuries suffered by the claimant, he was unable to cultivate the same resulting in deprival of the income generated from the land.

He further submitted that the finding regarding liability on the owner of the lorry/insurer and the owner of the car is upheld by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in MFA No.30201/2012 and therefore, the liability imposed by the Tribunal in this case cannot be, upset.

He further contends that the claimant suffered injuries and was on continuous treatment from 13.09.2008 till 24.02.2010, during which time, he underwent three procedures as an impatient for nearly 51 days.

Thus, he claimed that the Tribunal must have pragmatically assessed the disability suffered by the - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1368 claimant, more particularly, in view of the evidence of P.W.2 and P.W.3, who deposed that the claimant continues to suffer from abdominal related issues.
Learned counsel therefore, submitted that the disability assessed by the Tribunal deserves to be re-considered.
12. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the insurer/owner of the lorry, owner of the car and learned counsel for the claimant.
I have also perused the records of the Tribunal as well as its judgment and award.

13. In view of the finding recorded by this Court in MFA No.30201/2012, it has to be held that drivers of both the vehicles i.e., lorry and car were equally negligent and responsible for the accident.
The claimant was a passenger in the car.
He suffered injuries namely, fracture of medial mallelous of right tibia, lower 1/4th of fibula, fractures of 5th, 6th and 7th ribs on the right side and severe abdominal injuries.
However, there were no injuries to internal organs.
However, the discharge summary at Ex.P.11 - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1368 indicates blunt trauma of the abdomen with liver injury and jejunal blow out and sigmoid injury of colon.
The claimant underwent exploratory laparotomy with transverse loop colostomy and repair of the perforation in the intestine and colon.
These wounds were attributable to the injuries suffered by the claimant in the accident on 11.09.2008.

The repair of the colon further complicated, which resulted in a further treatment of the claimant between 11.02.2009 and 19.02.2009 and thereafter, between 16.02.2010 to 24.02.2010 for management of incisional hernia due to the surgery.

14. The assessment of the disability by the Tribunal at 10% was thoroughly unjustified in view of the fact that the claimant had suffered fracture of medial mallelous of right tibia, lower 1/4th of fibula Ganadhar S/O Ramchandra Koti vs Ashok S/O Kalyanrao And Ors on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94411683/
8 and three fractures of ribs on the right side and also other intestinal injuries.

sentences.text:
In the facts of this case,
taking into account the grievous nature of the injuries, this Court considers it appropriate to consider the disability suffered by the claimant at 20% to - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1368 the whole body.

The Tribunal committed an error in factoring 50% of the income towards loss of future prospects, though no material is placed on record to establish that the business undertaken by the claimant had suffered a loss.

In that view of the matter, the compensation to which the claimant is entitled to deserves to be re-determined as follows:

 3. Attendant and Rs.40,000/-

 to disability  (Rs.7,500/- x 12 x  15 x 20%)
 5. Loss of amenities Rs.50,000/-
 6. Loss of income Rs.45,000/-
 during laid up  period of 6 months  Total Rs.11,70,000/-

In view of the above, the appeal filed by the insurer of the lorry is allowed in part and 50% of loss of future prospects factored by the Tribunal is set aside.
The appeal filed by the owner of the Car does not merit consideration and same is dismissed.
The Cross-objection
filed by the claimant
is allowed in part.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal in a sum of Rs.9,03,000/- is enhanced to Rs.11,70,000/-.

sentences.text: The enhanced compensation shall be paid by the insurer of the lorry and owner of the car in the ratio of 50% each along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

The insurer of the lorry and owner of the car shall deposit the enhanced compensation and interest before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of a receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be kept in the name of the claimant in any Nationalized Bank for a period of three years.

 JUDGMENT MFA No.200706/2016 is filed by the insurer of one of the vehicles challenging the quantum of compensation while MFA No.200828/2016 is filed by the owner of one of the vehicles challenging the liability imposed upon him
opennyai_summary.facts:
The claimant contended that the injuries suffered by him was permanent and he had difficulty in digesting food.
He therefore,
claimed that he was permanently disabled and hence, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1368 Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of both the vehicles namely, the Car in which he was travelling and the lorry which was parked in the middle of the road.
3. The driver of the lorry was placed ex parte.
4. The insurer of the lorry contested the claim petition and denied the accident and claimed that the lorry was not parked in the middle of the road.
He claimed that as per the charge-sheet, the lorry was moving and the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the car.
In so far as the liability to pay compensation is concerned, it held that the drivers of both the vehicles were equally negligent and consequently, 50% of the liability was fastened upon the owner and insurer of the lorry and 50% of the liability was fastened upon the owner of the car.
It directed both of them to pay compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
opennyai_summary.arguments: He contended that if notional income as prescribed by this Court is applied, then the notional income of the claimant ought to have been considered at a sum of Rs.4,250/- per month.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
13. In view of the finding recorded by this Court in MFA No.30201/2012, it has to be held that drivers of both the vehicles i.e., lorry and car were equally negligent and responsible for the accident.
The claimant was a passenger in the car.
He suffered injuries namely, fracture of medial mallelous of right tibia, lower 1/4th of fibula, fractures of 5th, 6th and 7th ribs on the right side and severe abdominal injuries.
14. The assessment of the disability by the Tribunal at 10% was thoroughly unjustified in view of the fact that the claimant had suffered fracture of medial mallelous of right tibia, lower 1/4th of fibula Ganadhar S/O Ramchandra Koti vs Ashok S/O Kalyanrao And Ors on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94411683/
8 and three fractures of ribs on the right side and also other intestinal injuries.
The Tribunal committed an error in factoring 50% of the income towards loss of future prospects, though no material is placed on record to establish that the business undertaken by the claimant had suffered a loss.

In view of the above, the appeal filed by the insurer of the lorry is allowed in part and 50% of loss of future prospects factored by the Tribunal is set aside.
The appeal filed by the owner of the Car does not merit consideration and same is dismissed.
The Cross-objection
filed by the claimant
is allowed in part.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal in a sum of Rs.9,03,000/- is enhanced to Rs.11,70,000/-.
The enhanced compensation shall be paid by the insurer of the lorry and owner of the car in the ratio of 50% each along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
The insurer of the lorry and owner of the car shall deposit the enhanced compensation and interest before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of a receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be kept in the name of the claimant in any Nationalized Bank for a period of three years.
